articles.title: US Open tennis: Fritz and Keys in action after Potapova beats Anisimova on day seven – live
articles.summary: The latest third-round updates from Flushing Meadows. You can mail Niall and follow us on TikTok and Bluesky. Last night Serena and Venus Williams – with their combined age of 456 - blew a five-point lead in the deciding tie-break as their return to the grand slam doubles stage ended in defeat…
body: “Any sign of a dramatic Zheng comeback? No, is the short answer” – me, 35 minutes ago. I was wrong, and Zheng moves on to a last-16 meeting with either Iga Swiatek or Maria Bouzkova, who are up next on Grandstand.

“I always believed [I could win], I just kept fighting,” says Zheng, who found serving at 5-4 down the toughest moment. She talks about her injury layoff – “the worst few months of my career” – and says “hard work has paid off” for her and her team.

On second serve, Keys looks to clip the line with a cross-court shot … but misses. Zheng Qinwen has won from 5-0 down, breaking Keys’ serve three times in a row and saving a match point at 5-1 down. She looks elated, Keys can’t wait to get out of there. How on earth did she lose that match?

Zheng breaks Keys again! Madison Keys makes a better start here, the first serve speeding up, but Qinwen Zheng is locked in, turning the rallies in her favour – and when Keys misses a desperate effort down the line, she breaks again. Three in a row, six games in a row, and now she’ll serve for the match.

articles.title: South Africa finish strongly to take 2-1 series lead against All Blacks
articles.summary: South Africa eventually overpower a spirited New Zealand as the world champions came on strong in the final quarter in Soweto to take a 2-1 series lead.
body: South Africa eventually overpowered a spirited New Zealand, who could only outrun their hosts' set-piece power for so long, as the world champions came on strong in the final quarter in Soweto to take a 2-1 lead in a high-quality 'Greatest Rivalry' series.
The two sides traded two tries each in a tight first half, with New Zealand's composure and ambition with ball in hand stretching South Africa's onrushing defence.
The All Blacks sniffed a famous victory when Will Jordan chased after his own kick ahead and crossed for a 17-12 lead in the 55th minute.
But Jesse Kriel barged through Leroy Carter to cross at the other end shortly after and, reprieved, South Africa took full advantage.

articles.title: Vuelta a España: Marco Brenner wins stage 14 but extreme heat forces shorter stage 15
articles.summary: Mas retains red jersey; stage 15 to be shortened. Tadej Pogacar to miss rest of season after surgery. German Marco Brenner fought off Bahrain Victorious rider Santiago Buitrago to claim victory in stage 14 of the Vuelta a España – a first Grand Tour win both for the rider and his Tudor team.
body: In a climactic duel, Brenner tailed leader Buitrago ⁠into the last 500m and timed his kick superbly, gritting his teeth as he sped ahead during the ascent to Sierra de La Pandera, ultimately finishing one second ahead of the Colombian.

Overall leader Enric Mas (Movistar), finishing 22nd in the stage, gained around 25 seconds on veteran four-time Vuelta winner Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe), who slipped from second to third in the general classification behind Felix Gall of the Decathlon CMA CGM team. Gall trails Mas by 2:06 in the race for the red jersey.

Carlos Rodríguez (Netcompany Ineos) finished the stage third at the end of the 154.5km ride from Jaén to La Pandera. He moved up to eighth overall having started the day 17th in the general classification.

“I cannot really believe it yet,” said 24-year-old Brenner of his stage win. “I was struggling with some sickness earlier in the race and had a crash, but I really wanted to show myself and also my teammates that I can be ‌up there.”

body: The Clarets looked on course to finally get their campaign up and running when Aaron Ramsey fired them ahead in the 56th minute.

But City levelled in the 82nd minute through Rob Dickie before a stunning strike from the substitute Yu Hirakawa just as the match ticked into stoppage time made it three wins in a row for Michael Skubala’s side, who climbed into the top four.
Two late goals underscored West Ham ’s second home victory in the space of five days and a 3-0 win over Derby that was less decisive than the scoreline suggests.

articles.title: Pogacar to miss rest of season after Vuelta crash
articles.summary: Five-time Tour de France champion Tadej Pogacar will not race again this season after suffering injuries including a fracture in his neck at the Vuelta a Espana.
body: The injuries, which he suffered last month on the race's eighth stage, means the Slovenian will miss out on the chance to win the World Championships for a third year in a row.
He crashed out of the Vuelta from a dominant position as race leader and required surgery on a broken collarbone, and also suffered concussion, a "stable" fracture in his neck and multiple abrasions.

The 27-year-old, who was aiming to complete the set of Grand Tour titles, adding the Vuelta to his single Giro d'Italia victory and five Tour de France wins, was due to defend his rainbow jersey at the World Championships in Montreal later this month.
"Of course, this isn't the way I wanted my season to finish," Pogacar said in a statement released by his team, UAE Team Emirates-XRG.

articles.summary: Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland is set for a spell on the sidelines after picking up a "significant" hamstring injury in Saturday's Scottish Premiership victory over Motherwell.
body: The Scotland striker limped off after eight minutes at Ibrox, with his replacement Ryan Naderi scoring the only goal of the game shortly after.
Shankland - who signed from Hearts in May - has scored four goals in his first 10 Rangers appearances, but will now miss several weeks in a blow to Derek McInnes.
"It's a similar injury we think that he had at Hearts last January. That was a period of time that he was out with that.
"We'll get the scan done on Monday and see how it looks then rather than speculating. It's disappointing because he was leading the line and scoring a few goals in the last couple of games.

articles.title: New season, same flaw - Chelsea title hopes already under scrutiny
articles.summary: With 11 minutes remaining, Chelsea appeared to be cruising to victory in their WSL opener against Aston Villa. So how did they throw it away?
body: Yet, after 57 touches in the opposition box, 23 shots inside the area, hitting the crossbar and having another goal disallowed for offside, somehow they drew 1-1.
The statistics are alarming given they did everything right to win, except score more.
It is an issue that has reared its head on several occasions during manager Sonia Bompastor's time in charge and is why many have tipped rivals Arsenal to win the title this season.
While England international Lauren James oozed quality and summer signing Katie McCabe had a strong WSL debut, Chelsea's lack of ruthlessness in front of goal could prove costly.

articles.title: How cheaper buys outshone £125m Enzo Fernandez on Manchester City bow
articles.summary: Man City 1-0 Coventry: Erling Haaland’s header earned the hosts all three points but the Championship winners went close to claiming a shock draw
body: The previous time Enzo Fernandez had started a match, he exited in disgrace. A few weeks and £125m later, some Manchester City fans stood to applaud their most expensive debutant ever.

From being sent off in the World Cup final to being parachuted in for an unexpected start, it has been an eventful few weeks for the Argentinian. Relatively speaking, this was the calm after the storm.

The taunts from the Coventry fans as he was substituted are a sign of a growing notoriety, even if Fernandez was on his best behaviour as he turned in a performance that was more encouraging than astounding. Yet if City could thank one deadline-day signing for victory, it was not him but Gianluigi Donnarumma, who arrived at the end of the window last summer and who made three terrific saves.
But for Fernandez, it may have been a taste of things to come. Opposition supporters booed him, Erling Haaland scored, and City won at home to top the table.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers looks ahead to fatherhood after retirement
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers looks ahead to fatherhood after retirement originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here. As Aaron Rodgers nears retirement, he is looking forward to an experience he hasn't had before: fatherhood.
body: In May, he shared that the 2026-2027 NFL season will be his last in the league as he enters his 22nd season. Rodgers shared that he is going to step away from the spotlight and start his family.
“And I’m looking forward to a life of quiet after 22 years in the pros and three in college and getting my body healed up and working on a family,” he continued. “That’s what I’m looking forward to.”

Rodgers secretly got married to Brittani -- he hasn't publicly shared his wife's last name -- last June. He also credited her with helping him reconnect with his estranged family. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback shared photos of himself with his parents and his older brother, Luke Rodgers, in July.
“I’m definitely excited about it,” said Rodgers. “I mean, being back in my family’s lives, and I’m having a lot of fun being Uncle Aaron.”

articles.title: Springboks edge thriller to take 2-1 lead in All Blacks series
articles.summary: South Africa came from behind to edge New Zealand 29-24 in a ferocious third Test that moved them 2-1 ahead in the 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' series with one game remaining.
body: The Springboks and All Blacks traded four tries apiece in a pulsating contest that was as brutal as it was captivating in front of a capacity crowd of 87,976 in Soweto.

Kurt-Lee Arendse, Jesse Kriel and Malcolm Marx crossed for the Springboks, who were also awarded a penalty try, as they followed last week's narrow victory in Cape Town with another hard-fought triumph.

New Zealand captain Ardie Savea scored two first-half tries before suffering a game-ending shoulder injury, while record try-scorer Will Jordan and hooker Samisoni Taukei'aho crossed late on for the All Blacks.

The teams now travel to Baltimore, USA, for the final instalment of the four-Test series, live on Sky Sports, where nothing less than victory will do for the All Blacks if they are to salvage something.

articles.summary: Lyndon Dykes scored his first two goals for injury-hit Millwall as they returned to winning ways in the Sky Bet Championship in some style with a 4-0 victory over Bolton at The Den.
body: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Millwall and Bolton Wanderers at The Den on Saturday; Lyndon Dykes scores twice in Lions win as both sides finish with 10 men.
The Lions made light of the fact they have 11 first team players currently unavailable - and that their last two games ended in heavy defeat - as they inflicted a third loss in a row on the Trotters.

A late burst of three goals in nine minutes gave the final score an emphatic look, while both teams finished with 10 men after Millwall midfielder Jenson Metcalfe and Bolton captain Josh Sheehan were sent off for violent conduct.
Bolton had a big chance to grab an early lead when Sam Dalby played a one-two with Sheehan before scuffing wide from inside the box.
